title: An AI-enabled structural atlas decodes kinase specificity across the human proteome - Nature Biotechnology
gist: KinoPlex uses ~20,000 AlphaFold structures plus positive-unlabeled learning to score all ~1.8 million human S/T/Y residues for structural phospho-competency, then intersects them with ~300 kinase PSSMs to yield ~250,000 high-confidence kinase-substrate candidates. Its central finding is that linear motif matching alone is nearly useless for predicting phosphorylation — ~47% of predicted non-phosphorylated sites still clear a kinase's 99th-percentile motif threshold — and that kinases split into 'positive-selecting' and 'negative-selecting' classes based on the structural accessibility of their preferred motifs. The atlas is hosted commercially by Cell Signaling Technology/PhosphoSitePlus and its senior authors sit across a dense web of kinase-oncology startups.

insights.claim: Only 6% of the 1.8 million serine/threonine/tyrosine residues in the human proteome have experimentally validated phosphorylation, and only 5% of those (roughly 0.3% of all sites) have been assigned to a specific kinase.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The addressable annotation gap in kinase signaling is ~99.7% of sites, which is the size of the market that computational phospho-atlases and mass-spec platform vendors are competing to fill.
insights.quote: Of the 1.8 million serine/threonine/tyrosine residues in the human proteome, only 6% bear experimental validation of phosphorylation, and only 5% of these have been mapped to a kinase.
insights.locator: Abstract, first sentence

insights.claim: The training set imbalance is extreme — roughly 100,880 known phosphosites against 1,367,324 uncharacterized serine/threonine residues — forcing the authors to use positive-unlabeled rather than standard supervised classification.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Any biology-ML company claiming supervised phospho-site prediction is training on a negative class that is contaminated with true positives; PU-learning competence is a real technical differentiator to diligence.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 1c, Known sites (blue, n = 100,880)

insights.claim: Known phosphosites are systematically enriched in disordered, solvent-accessible and low-packing-density regions, and fall into two distinct regimes: a dominant high-disorder/high-accessibility basin and a secondary structured-yet-surface-exposed mode.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Drug programs targeting phospho-dependent interactions should expect most real sites to sit in disordered, undruggable-by-pocket regions, favoring degrader/PPI-disruptor modalities over classic active-site chemistry.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 1e, Joint Density Analysis of Solvent Accessibility

insights.claim: KinoPlex extracts 3D structural features — half-sphere exposure, packing density, hydroxyl-specific SASA, pocket geometry, non-covalent interactions and electrostatics — for every S/T/Y residue in >20,000 AlphaFold v2 human protein models, and identifies ~567,000 residues as structurally phospho-competent.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: AlphaFold's commercial value keeps compounding downstream: predicted structures are now precise enough to serve as the substrate for proteome-scale PTM feature engineering, not just fold prediction.
insights.locator: Abstract; Extended Data Fig. 1a AlphaFold Database Protein Structure Acquisition

insights.claim: Intersecting structural competency with ~300 kinase position-specific scoring matrices narrows ~567,000 competent residues to ~250,000 high-confidence candidates that combine sequence recognition potential with optimal structural presentation.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A ~250k-entry ranked substrate list is directly usable as a target-discovery funnel for kinase-inhibitor and biomarker programs that previously had no way to prioritize unannotated sites.
insights.locator: Abstract; Extended Data Fig. 2a Global Kinase PSSM Scoring

insights.claim: Kinase PSSM score distributions were calibrated by bootstrapping 100,000 randomly sampled sites per kinase against a proteome-wide background rather than a curated phosphosite background, which is what allows cross-kinase percentile comparison at scale.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Scoring against the full proteome instead of known-site sets is the methodological choice that makes the atlas defensible; competing tools using curated backgrounds will inherit annotation bias.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 2a, the score distribution was bootstrapped

insights.claim: Roughly 47% of sites KinoPlex predicts are never phosphorylated still exceed the 99th-percentile motif score for at least one kinase, versus ~60% of known sites and ~50% of predicted-phosphorylated sites — meaning consensus-motif hits barely discriminate real substrates.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Every substrate-prediction product built on motif scanning alone is close to a coin flip; structural context is the moat, and vendors without it should be discounted.
insights.quote: underscoring that linear motif alone is insufficient to determine phosphorylability without structural context
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 3e, Proportion of Site Predictions At High-Scoring Kinase Thresholds

insights.claim: Across the kinome, an average of ~65% of a kinase's top-1% motif matches sit in structurally phospho-incompetent environments, with a range of ~12% to ~95% depending on the kinase.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Kinase-specific incompetency rates are a quantitative screen for which kinases have tractable, well-defined substrate sets — a prioritization signal for target selection in kinase drug discovery.
insights.quote: about half of near-consensus motifs lie in structures that are unlikely to be phosphorylated
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 4, Kinome-Wide Summary of Kinase Structural Selectivity

insights.claim: TTBK1's best motif matches are strongly enriched for structurally incompetent sites while CMGC-family kinases show marked enrichment for competent sites, indicating opposite 'self-selection logic' between kinase families.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: TTBK1 programs (tau/neurodegeneration adjacent) face a substrate-inference problem that CMGC programs do not; expect higher false-positive rates in TTBK1 substrate claims.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 4, Extremes illustrate the divergence

insights.claim: Kinases achieve specificity in two opposite ways: negative-selecting kinases prefer motifs that are structurally scarce or occluded, while positive-selecting kinases become promiscuous because their preferred motif is structurally accessible — specificity is therefore not set by motif discrimination alone.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A new axis for predicting inhibitor selectivity and off-pathway toxicity: positive-selecting kinases will have broader real substrate footprints and thus broader on-target-but-off-pathway effects.
insights.quote: kinases achieve specificity through structural scarcity of their preferred motif (negative-selecting kinases) or promiscuity through its structural accessibility (positive-selecting kinases), rather than by motif discrimination alone
insights.locator: Abstract, sequence–structure selective coupling

insights.claim: The negative/positive selection split shows up at the motif level: BRAF's preferred WLXXS motif sits in high-pLDDT, low-disorder, low-SASA, highly packed contexts, whereas ERK1's PXXSP motif is skewed toward disordered, exposed, loosely packed contexts.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Within a single drugged pathway (RAF-MEK-ERK), the two nodes have structurally opposite substrate logic — relevant to why ERK inhibition produces broader pathway effects than BRAF inhibition.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 7c, Motifs favored by negatively-selecting kinases

insights.claim: Some motifs are depleted in the whole proteome yet enriched among known phosphosites, a pattern the authors call structural compensation — rare sequences survive as functional sites when their structural context is unusually permissive.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Rare-motif substrates are systematically under-discovered by frequency-based screens, a source of novel targets hiding in low-abundance sequence space.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 6b, Whole-Proteome versus Phosphoproteome enrichment

insights.claim: Even among the most abundant +1-proline motifs targeted by CMGC kinases, there is significant variability in disorder, so motif class does not collapse to a single structural profile.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Substrate prediction for CDK/MAPK-class kinases needs site-level structure, not motif-class heuristics — a direct argument for structure-aware tooling in oncology target ID.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 6d, Proline-Directed Kinases Motifs Adopt Structurally Distinct

insights.claim: Clustering kinases by the mean structural feature vector of their predicted substrate pools yields seven primary clusters that are family-biased but overlapping, described as microenvironment 'dialects' of substrate recognition rather than clean family boundaries.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Structural clustering gives a non-sequence-based map of which kinases will share substrates — a better prior for predicting polypharmacology than kinome phylogeny.
insights.quote: revealing family-biased yet overlapping microenvironment “dialects” of substrate recognition
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 5, Structure-derived relationships among kinase groups

insights.claim: Substrate-pool sizes differ sharply across families in the atlas — CMGC 2,445, AGC 1,635, CAMK 1,393, Other 1,244, CK1 839, Atypical 715, STE 380 and TKL 260 — so statistical power for substrate inference is very uneven across the kinome.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Claims about TKL and STE kinase substrates rest on an order of magnitude less data than CMGC claims; weight due diligence accordingly.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 3, Sample sizes of families include AGC = 1635

insights.claim: Kinase family structural preferences diverge significantly on pLDDT, SASA and disorder score, meaning a kinase's family predicts the ordered-versus-disordered character of the sites it can actually reach.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Family-level structural signatures let you triage which kinase a newly observed phosphosite plausibly came from without any wet-lab work.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 3a-c, Kinase Family-Specific Structural Signatures

insights.claim: Sequence-structure coupling is compartment aware and evolutionarily conserved: for FAM20C, high-scoring motifs are equally available in secreted and non-secreted proteins, yet only secreted, structurally competent sites show elevated positional conservation at +0 and +2 matching the SxE consensus.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Localization is an independent filter on kinase-substrate assignment; substrate predictions that ignore compartment will over-call targets, which matters for secreted-proteome and biomineralization-linked drug programs.
insights.quote: Only in secreted proteins do we observe significantly elevated conservation at +0 and +2, consistent with the SxE consensus for FAM20C.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 9b, Positional conservation is specifically enriched

insights.claim: The authors explicitly ruled out the trivial sequence-prevalence explanation for FAM20C's secretome bias by showing near-identical motif threshold-crossing rates in secreted and non-secreted cohorts with no statistically significant difference.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The control strengthens the case that structural/localization gating — not motif abundance — drives specificity, raising confidence in the framework's generalization to other compartmentalized kinases.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 9a, Comparable availability of high-scoring motifs

insights.claim: Predictions were validated with ultra-deep LC/LC-MS/MS DIA phosphoproteomics on the Astral platform in K562 chronic myelogenous leukemia cells, confirming de novo sites and letting kinase activity be inferred from identification-only evidence without quantitative comparison.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Inferring kinase activity from identification-only MS data lowers the cost and sample burden of kinase-activity profiling, expanding the addressable market for high-resolution MS instruments.
insights.locator: Fig. 6: Ultra-deep phosphoproteomics validates KinoPlex predictions

insights.claim: Spearman correlations between 303 inferred kinase activities and drug sensitivity across cancer cell lines produce a 303-dimensional rank fingerprint per drug that clusters mechanistically related compounds — demonstrated with trametinib.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A kinase-activity fingerprint that groups drugs by mechanism is a repositioning and combination-design tool, and a way to flag undisclosed mechanisms in competitors' clinical assets.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 10, Trametinib drug similarity analysis

insights.claim: In the same framework high kinase activity can predict either resistance or sensitivity depending on the kinase, giving a directional, per-kinase readout rather than a single activity score.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Per-kinase directional signal is the raw material for patient-stratification biomarkers in kinase-inhibitor trials.
insights.quote: Red indicates high rank (positive correlation: high kinase activity predicts drug resistance)
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 10, Heatmap values

insights.claim: The K562 model system is Philadelphia-chromosome positive CML, and the paper's reference framing points at TAM-family receptor tyrosine kinases including TYRO3 as candidate myeloid leukemia dependencies surfaced by the atlas.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: TAM-family inhibitors in CML are a small but identifiable thesis; watch for follow-on programs citing this atlas as target rationale.
insights.locator: References, TAM family kinases are potential candidate targets

insights.claim: The interactive KinoPlex atlas and its code are hosted by Cell Signaling Technology on PhosphoSitePlus at kinoplex.phosphosite.org, placing a private reagent company at the distribution layer of a proteome-wide public dataset.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: CST converts an academic atlas into a funnel for phospho-specific antibody and reagent sales — the classic data-to-consumables flywheel in life-science tools.
insights.quote: An interactive portal for browsing the atlas is hosted by Cell Signaling Technology/PhosphoSitePlus at kinoplex.phosphosite.org.
insights.locator: Data availability

insights.claim: The senior authors carry an unusually dense commercial web around kinase biology — Lewis Cantley is a founder of Agios Pharmaceuticals with equity in Cell Signaling Technologies, Volastra, Larkspur and 1 Base Pharmaceuticals plus cofounder stakes in Marendis Therapeutics and Faeth Therapeutics, while Steven Gygi sits on the Thermo Fisher Scientific and CST scientific advisory boards.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Maps who is positioned to commercialize kinase-substrate atlases first; Marendis appears three times across the author list and is the concentrated bet on this specific framework.
insights.locator: Competing interests

insights.claim: Three separate authors — Jared Johnson, Tomer Yaron-Barir and Lewis Cantley — are cofounders and shareholders in Marendis Therapeutics, the same team behind the prior human serine/threonine and tyrosine kinome specificity atlases that supply KinoPlex's PSSMs.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Marendis holds the upstream motif asset and the downstream structural layer; it is the private vehicle most directly levered to kinase-specificity IP.
insights.locator: Competing interests; Code availability

insights.claim: All primary assets were released openly — raw MS files on MassIVE (MSV000099698), the full structural atlas and proteome-wide PSSM percentiles on Zenodo, and feature-extraction code on GitHub — so the moat is the portal and the reagents, not the data.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Open data means fast-following competitors can rebuild the atlas; value accrues to whoever owns the interface, the antibodies and the follow-on validation, not the file.
insights.locator: Data availability; Code availability
